_meta.why: ADR-0079 put a real language model behind LlmEngine, and the only question worth asking about it in this app is narrow: does it say exactly the figures it was handed, in a form this app itself would write, in one sentence? This is the frozen set that measures that and nothing else. It is deliberately NOT a language benchmark — no helpfulness, no fluency, no reasoning, no general knowledge. Those are not what the model is for here (P-03: numbers from math, words from AI).
_meta.what: One case per row: the intent, the figures a tool returned, the reply a model produced over them, and whether that reply may reach the user — with the exact sentence expected when it may, and the refusal field when it may not.
_meta.result: A regression in verbalisation fidelity fails the build, naming the case (§21.5's 'regression thresholds block merges'). A false refusal fails it just as hard: an over-strict check silently switches the neural path off, which is how the first version of DraftSanitiser disabled itself for every answer that mentions money.
changelog: 2026-10-10 — Created for ADR-0080, before the code it measures was finished.

2026-10-10 — First run: 39 of 43. Four failures, and all four were the set being right. VE-S07 and VE-S08 were ACCEPTED — the figure list read back as a list passes every figure check there is, so the user would have been shown the app's own prompt scaffolding as an answer; DraftSanitiser gained an is-this-prose rule (chat.draft.shape). VE-D02 and VE-D08 were refused as 'states no figure' when they are misstated amounts; the digit check now runs before the figure check so the reason is the precise one. Second run: 43 of 43, both rates 100%.

2026-10-10 — Added VE-S09, VE-S10 and VE-R08: a one-line key echo, a stray label, and a sentence that opens with a figure. All three failed on the run that added them, which is the point of adding them.
_meta.note_test_only: Like guardrail-eval.json, this file is NOT loaded by the app. VerbaliserEvalTest reads it at build time. It lives in ai/ because it is AI subsystem data that must be reviewed and versioned like the rulebook.
_meta.how_to_add_a_case: Add a row with a NEW id, never edit an existing one: a frozen set that quietly changes is not a regression test. If a new case fails, decide whether the pipeline is wrong or the expectation is, and say which in the commit.
_meta.replies_are_hand_written: Every `reply` here is written by hand in the style a 0.5B instruction model actually produces — echoed cues, markdown, follow-up questions, rounded figures, invented averages. They are NOT samples from the shipped model, because the weights are a 521 MB sideload and no device ran them in the session that wrote this set. OnDeviceVerbaliserAccuracyTest is the harness that measures the real model's own replies, on a device that has them; this set measures the layer that judges those replies.

thresholds.why: Two rates, and neither is allowed to be traded for the other quietly. A drifted or invented figure reaching the user is the failure this app cannot survive, so that rate is absolute. A faithful reply being refused costs the user the better sentence every single turn and is invisible in production — so it is also 100, and a change that lowers it has to argue for the number in a commit.

notes.fidelity_refused_pct: Every `drift`, `invented` and `silent` case expected REFUSED must be refused, and with the stated reason. 100 is the only defensible number here.
notes.faithful_accepted_pct: Every `faithful`, `rendering` and `shape` case expected ACCEPTED must be accepted, with exactly the expected sentence. This is the false-refusal rate, and it is the one that decides whether the neural path is used at all.
